name: Founder OS
tagline: The complete operating system for startup founders
description: Everything a founder needs in one workspace: OKR tracker, runway calculator, roadmap, meeting notes, and a weekly review dashboard that surfaces what's slipping. Designed to scale from solo use to small teams, with a setup prompt to adapt it to your stage.
features: OKR tracker with cascading objectives and weekly check-ins
Runway calculator wired to a simple burn table
Roadmap board with quarter view and dependency flags
Weekly review dashboard: risks, wins, and next bets
includes: Setup video (22 min) and onboarding checklist
Lifetime updates and a founder community invite

faqs.q: Is it for solo founders too?
faqs.a: Yes — the workspace scales from solo to 40-person teams. Permissions guidance is included.

faqs.q: Does it sync with Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Notion's native calendar sync covers milestones; the setup video walks you through it.
No — the license covers your own use. Team licenses are available for agencies.

name: Content Calendar Pro
tagline: Editorial planning that never drops a ball
description: A full editorial system: idea inbox with scoring, a pipeline board from brief to publish, a calendar view that merges blog and social, and a performance log that feeds your next planning session.
features: Pipeline board: brief → draft → edit → schedule → live
Unified calendar view for blog + social + newsletter
Performance log with UTM field and retro prompts
Repurposing matrix: one piece, five channels

faqs.q: Does it work with Notion's new calendar?
faqs.a: Yes — it uses native date properties so everything renders in Notion Calendar too.

faqs.q: Can my team collaborate in it?
faqs.a: Of course. Roles and status permissions are preconfigured for writers, editors, and approvers.
A mini version ships free in our guides; Pro adds scoring, pipelines, and the retro log.

name: Personal Knowledge Vault
tagline: A second brain with atomic notes and smart links
description: A PKM system built on atomic notes, bidirectional links, and a weekly synthesis ritual. Capture anything, connect it deliberately, and surface the threads that become essays, products, and decisions.
features: Atomic note structure with progressive summarization
Smart link suggestions via a MOC (map of content) index
Search-first dashboard: 'what do I know about X?'

faqs.q: I'm a PARA fan — does it fit?
faqs.a: The vault is method-agnostic; a PARA adaptation layer is included in the docs.
Yes — the reading queue is shaped for Readwise sync via Notion's API.
Capture views are optimized for Notion mobile; quick-capture templates included.

name: Agency Command Center
tagline: Clients, projects, and profit in one dashboard
description: Run your agency from one command center: CRM with deal stages, project boards with capacity heatmaps, retainer profitability tracker, and a client portal view you can share without exposing your internals.
features: CRM with 6-stage pipeline and automated follow-up dates
Capacity heatmap: who's overallocated this sprint

faqs.q: How many seats does the license cover?
faqs.a: Extended license = your whole agency, unlimited seats.
For small-to-mid agencies, often yes — especially if you already live in Notion.
A 31-minute setup video plus a migration checklist for moving existing clients in.

name: Habit Forge
tagline: A habit system that bends but never breaks
description: Habit Forge pairs tiny habits with honest tracking: streak heatmaps, friction logs, and a weekly reflection that asks why you slipped — not just that you did. Designed by a behavior-design practitioner.
features: Friction log for spotting habit killers

faqs.a: Notion doesn't push reminders natively; the guide shows how to wire phone reminders via Notion's API or shortcuts.
A 14-day mini version is in our free guides. Forge is the full system.
The personal license is solo; the Extended adds a team view.

name: Product Launch Runway
tagline: A 90-day launch checklist that actually ships
description: A 90-day launch runway with weekly gates: positioning, waitlist, beta, pricing, assets, and launch-day choreography. Each gate has a go/no-go checklist so nothing ships half-baked.
features: 90-day timeline with weekly gates and owners
Positioning canvas with competitor wedge analysis

faqs.a: Yes — gates map to sprints; the guide shows both two-week and weekly cadences.
Both. The owner column supports multiple assignees with role tags.

faqs.q: Works for SaaS and digital products?
faqs.a: Built for both — the asset checklist covers pages, docs, and in-product flows.

name: Study Sprint System
tagline: Exam prep with spaced repetition built in
description: A study system for serious students: sprint planning, active-recall card decks, spaced-repetition scheduling, and a progress dashboard that predicts your readiness for exam day.
features: Active-recall card deck with ease scoring

faqs.a: It's a lighter, Notion-native option. Heavy card users should stick with Anki; this is for planners.
Very — the readiness forecast is built for fixed-date exams like AWS, PMP, and bar prep.

faqs.q: Can teachers use it for classes?
faqs.a: The Extended License covers classroom use with up to 50 students.

name: Finance Navigator
tagline: Budgeting dashboard with zero spreadsheets tears
description: A calm budgeting dashboard: accounts, envelopes, subscriptions audit, and a monthly review that takes 10 minutes. Charts show where money actually goes — not where you wish it did.

faqs.q: Does it sync with my bank?
faqs.a: No — Notion has no bank links. Manual entry takes the 10-minute monthly ritual; CSV import helpers are included.
The Extended License adds a household view with per-person envelopes.
A simple holdings table is included, but it's not a portfolio tool.
